content.title: Recommendations for cardiogenic shock (selected page)
content.summary: Early revascularization (PCI or CABG) is recommended for patients with AMI complicated by cardiogenic shock (CS). Routine use of intra-aortic balloon pump (IABP) is not recommended because it was not associated with lower 30-day mortality in randomized trial data. The role of mechanical circulatory support (MCS) devices such as veno-arterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (VA-ECMO) and micro-axial pumps in AMI with CS is not well established; randomized data are limited and observational data suggest possible increased adverse events with some intravascular left ventricular (LV) assist devices compared with IABP. MCS may be considered in selected patients with severe/refractory CS, but caution is advised until further randomized data are available.
recommendations: Early revascularization with either PCI or CABG is recommended for patients with AMI complicated by cardiogenic shock, based on the SHOCK trial.

Proceed to PCI at the time of diagnostic angiography if myocardial revascularization is indicated; surgical revascularization is an option if PCI of the infarct-related artery (IRA) has failed or anatomy is not amenable to PCI.
Routine use of IABP is not recommended for CS complicating AMI (IABP-SHOCK II trial: no lower 30-day mortality).
The role of other mechanical circulatory devices (VA-ECMO, micro-axial pumps) in AMI with CS is not established; large randomized trials are warranted.
VA-ECMO immediate implementation did not show improved outcomes in the referenced randomized trial, but interpretation is limited by crossover and heterogeneity.

Observational analyses report that some intravascular LV assist devices may be associated with increased risk of adverse events (including mortality and bleeding) compared with IABP; exercise caution and consider MCS only in selected patients until further randomized data are available.

key_trials.trial: SHOCK (Should We Emergently Revascularize Occluded Coronaries for Cardiogenic Shock)
key_trials.population: Patients with AMI complicated by cardiogenic shock
key_trials.finding: Supports early revascularization (PCI or CABG) in AMI with CS
key_trials.notes: Used as basis for recommending early revascularization

key_trials.trial: IABP-SHOCK II (Intraaortic Balloon Pump in Cardiogenic Shock II)
key_trials.population: Patients with cardiogenic shock complicating AMI
key_trials.finding: IABP use was not associated with lower 30-day mortality
key_trials.notes: Therefore routine use of IABP is not recommended in this setting

key_trials.trial: Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation in the Therapy of Cardiogenic Shock (randomized trial)
key_trials.population: 122 patients (51% with STEMI) with rapidly deteriorating or severe CS
key_trials.finding: Immediate implementation of VA-ECMO did not result in improved clinical outcomes
key_trials.notes: Interpretation limited by ~40% crossover to VA-ECMO in conservative arm, heterogenous CS phenotypes, and crossover in combined primary endpoint

devices_and_roles.role: Preferred immediate revascularization approach when indicated at diagnostic angiography
Valuable option when PCI of the IRA has failed or coronary anatomy is not amenable to PCI
Not routinely recommended for CS complicating AMI (no mortality benefit in IABP-SHOCK II)
Potential option for rapidly deteriorating/severe CS but evidence limited and trial did not show improved outcomes; interpretation complicated by crossover

devices_and_roles.device: Micro-axial pumps / intravascular LV assist devices
devices_and_roles.role: Role not well established; observational data suggest increased adverse events (mortality, bleeding) compared with IABP in some analyses

clinical_cautions: Large-scale randomized trials on MCS in AMI with CS are warranted before broad recommendations can be made.
Observational signals of increased adverse events with some LV assist devices warrant caution; consider MCS only in selected patients with ACS and severe/refractory CS.
Management of CS complicating AMI with multivessel disease (MVD) is addressed elsewhere (referenced Section 10).
references_in_text: SHOCK trial (reference numbers indicated in text)
